title: Closing Out the Lawn Season in Eastern Iowa
meta_title: Closing Out the Lawn Season in Eastern Iowa
meta_description: A look back at what the fall season should have covered by now, and a look ahead at what winter planning looks like for eastern Iowa lawns and sprinklers.
lede: By the end of November, the active lawn season in eastern Iowa is essentially over. Here's a checkpoint on where things should stand.
excerpt: A season-end checkpoint on lawn and irrigation prep heading into winter.

sections.heading: Where the Lawn Should Be
paragraphs: By now, established lawns should be dormant, and any sod installed this fall should have had at least several weeks of root growth before the first hard freeze, which typically hit eastern Iowa early to mid October. If your lawn has browned off for winter, that's the expected, normal end to the season.

sections.heading: Where the Irrigation System Should Be
paragraphs: The sprinkler system should have been winterized before that same first freeze. If it wasn't, the priority now is getting a blowout done as soon as possible to limit further damage from additional freezes over the rest of winter, rather than waiting for spring.

sections.heading: What Winter Actually Looks Like From Here
paragraphs: Once dormancy has set in and the irrigation system is squared away, there isn't much active lawn work left until spring. Winter is a quiet stretch for both the grass and the system, which makes it a reasonable time to start thinking ahead instead.

sections.heading: Starting to Think About Spring
paragraphs: Spring projects, whether that's a new lawn, an irrigation install, or general planning, tend to get busy fast once the weather turns. Using the quiet winter months to think through what you want done in spring means you're not starting from scratch once the season opens back up.

faqs.q: Is it normal for the whole lawn to be brown by the end of November?
faqs.a: Yes. Established grass goes dormant for winter, and brown, non-growing turf is the expected state at this point in the season.

faqs.q: What if my irrigation system still isn't winterized by now?
faqs.a: Get a blowout done as soon as possible. It won't undo any damage from an early freeze, but it prevents additional damage from further freezes over the rest of winter.

faqs.q: Is there anything to actively do for the lawn over winter?
faqs.a: Not much. Winter is a quiet period for lawn care. It's a reasonable time to start planning spring projects instead.
